security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and system reconnaissance findings are false positives from Markdown examples. Require explicit user confirmation before changing temperature, alarms, audio, power, or base angle.

content.user_title: Control Eight Sleep Pods with eightctl
content.value_statement: Managing pod settings through a terminal can be error-prone and repetitive. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use eightctl safely for common Eight Sleep tasks.
actual_capabilities: Check Eight Sleep pod status through the eightctl CLI.
Turn the pod on or off when the user approves the action.
Set pod temperature with the eightctl temp command.
List, create, update, or dismiss alarms and schedules supported by eightctl.
Control supported audio and base angle commands exposed by eightctl.
Use documented config or environment credentials for eightctl authentication.
limitations: Requires the eightctl binary and valid Eight Sleep account credentials.
Uses an unofficial and rate-limited API, so frequent logins should be avoided.
Needs user confirmation before changing temperature, alarms, power, audio, or base angle.
Does not replace Eight Sleep support, safety guidance, or device warranty terms.

use_cases.title: Check Bed Readiness
use_cases.description: Review pod status before sleep and confirm whether the device is online and configured as expected.

use_cases.title: Prepare Night Settings
use_cases.description: Set a target temperature and verify the active schedule before bedtime.

use_cases.title: Manage Shared Schedules
use_cases.description: Review alarms and schedule changes with confirmation before updating household sleep settings.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pod Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use eightctl to check my Eight Sleep pod status. Summarize the current state without changing any settings.

prompt_templates.title: Set Bedtime Temperature
prompt_templates.prompt: Set my Eight Sleep pod temperature to 20 only after confirming with me. Show the planned command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Review Alarms
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Eight Sleep alarms and identify any active wake alarms. Ask before creating, updating, or dismissing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Sleep Routine Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pod status, schedules, alarms, audio state, and base settings. Recommend changes, but wait for approval before any device action.

output_examples.input: Check whether my pod is ready for tonight.
output_examples.output: The pod status was checked. It is online, and no settings were changed.
I will change the pod temperature to 20 after your confirmation. No command has been run yet.
The current alarms were listed. I found active alarms and will ask before making any changes.

best_practices: Confirm every state-changing command before execution.
Use secure credential storage and redact secrets from terminal output.
Avoid repeated logins because the unofficial API is rate-limited.
anti_patterns: Do not run temperature, alarm, audio, power, or base commands without approval.
Do not print config files or credential environment variables in chat.
Do not build polling loops that repeatedly log in or hammer the API.

faq.question: Does this skill require eightctl to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects the eightctl binary to be available before commands can run.

faq.question: Can it control pod temperature?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use eightctl temp, but it should ask before changing temperature.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The skill documents a config file and EIGHTCTL_EMAIL and EIGHTCTL_PASSWORD environment variables for eightctl authentication.

faq.question: Does it use the official Eight Sleep API?
faq.answer: No. The skill notes that the API is unofficial and rate-limited.

faq.question: Can it manage alarms and schedules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list and modify supported alarms and schedules through eightctl commands.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: Status checks can run directly. Device changes should wait for explicit user confirmation.
